restrictions: Target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..37 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct complete 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; every output is checked with the target before it is returned.

Construction: the two-block attack of ePrint 2026/1120 (38-step characteristic of its Table 3, two-bit conditions of Table 4, published semi-free-start pair of Table 5) with the published A3..A13, E7..E13, W11..W15, and the first three dense-part words (A0, A1, A2) replaced by dense-part variants: 256 fixed A0 values, the 768-value A2 list, and every A1 for which the variant is valid (exact test: E cells of rows 4..8 and the published dW_i, ds0(W_i) for i = 8..11). Lemma 3 (proof.md 4.1): every valid variant reproduces all A/E cells of rows -4..15 and every modular and s0/s1 difference reaching rows >= 16 (the XOR cells of W7..W11 need not hold). 2^37.48061 variants per chaining value.

Row 16 by table: W16 = s0(Y + A1) - A1 + Z0 + c9(A2) where (Y, Z0) depends only on (CV1, A0) (Lemma 5); row 16 holds iff W16 is in a set G of exactly 32 words (exhaustive). Table T_j (one per A0) lists, for each (Y, Z0), every valid (A1, A2) whose W16 is one of the 22 words of G for which row 17 can hold (for the other 10 no E17 passes row 17; exact count, proof.md Appendix C); at most 236,544 entries per bucket (Lemma 6). Each entry is then tested exactly: W7 in F7 (|F7| = 287,309,824), rows 17..37 of both members (every cell, + pair and two-bit condition).

Cost: fixed caps. N_G = 390,749,047,013,370,053,791 groups (2^68.40480), each one first-block compression and 256 A0 blocks in packs of four; caps NE_MAX, NW_MAX, N1_MAX, N2_MAX on entries, W7 passes, first-row-17-test passes and deep paths, tested after every group (one group's overshoot charged; Hoeffding over the independent groups). Counted program (experiments/vt38.py, op-counting word-RAM interpreter; counts asserted at every run): prologue 95 + 1 unit, pack of four blocks 61, entry 6, W7 pass 46, A17 tests 28, deep path at most 3,155, epilogue and loop 19; preprocessing as counted code: enumeration (67 per candidate, 38 per valid variant), table construction (150 + 240 per (Y, variant), 4 + 8 + 10 per header): 2^67.07859 units. Allowances A_C = 2^70, A_S = 2^70, DEV = 2^64 (margins in H4) are 49.3% of T; the attack proper is 2^71.05. Exact total 2^72.031945 (cert.py, proof.md 7), claimed 72.03195.

Success probability at least 0.3900004 under H1 (chaining value of one trial behaves as uniform), H2 (variant-averaged q3 >= q3_model = 2^-102, about one bit below the preregistered SMC bounds on independent streams: 2^-101.0101 over a uniform 2^20-variant sample, 2^-101.0051 over 256 fresh uniform variants; 1,883,203 tail successes all rebuilt as verified 38-step semi-free-start collisions) and H5 (expected number of further successes in a group seen from a success <= 1; measured about 0.0018; Bonferroni). N_G = ceil(0.494297 / q_lb) with 0.494297 = -ln(1 - 0.39) rounded up at the 6th decimal: no slack (0ae69bcb's 0.396 target padded N_G by 2%). Groups use fresh coins and are independent; nothing is assumed independent inside a group. No expected-work bound and no independence-of-conditions model is used.

Memory (a reported metric): at most 2^80.117 bytes, dominated by the 256 tables (2^64 header words and 2 x 22 x 2^32 x |R_j| entry words each); claimed 2^80.12. The claim is a time bound in the track's word-RAM model, not a practical memory budget. baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score.

heuristics.statement: For one group, the chaining value CV1 = F_38(IV, M0) of a uniform first block M0 behaves as a uniform 256-bit value as far as the events of one fixed variant are concerned: for each A0 the table index (Y, Z0) is uniform (so a bucket holds |R_j| 2^-27 entries in expectation), W7 is uniform and independent of (W0, W1) (so a bucket entry passes the W7 filter with p2 = 2^-3.90197), and the second-block words have the distribution of proof.md Section 3.5 and Lemma 4. A statement about one first block and one variant at a time; nothing is assumed about two variants of one group (H5).
heuristics.scope: The per-variant success probability p2 q3(v), the expectations of the three work counters (caps NE_MAX, NW_MAX, N1_MAX) and hence N_G and the success bound. Not the validity of any output: every output is checked with the target.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured on 5.2 x 10^7 real first blocks (uniform M0 through real 38-step compressions; pipe.c, proof.md 6.3) for four A0 of the set: entries per chaining value within 0.07% of |R_j| 2^-27 (5.5920, 5.5903, 5.5733, 5.5945 against 5.5939, 5.5939, 5.5727, 5.5939), W7 rates within 0.003 bit of 2^-3.90197, row 17 passed 156 times against 148.4 predicted; 0 cell mismatches in about 2.9 x 10^8 constructed pairs. On 400 real chaining values with their true buckets (2,326 entries) the counters of 0ae69bcb's counted program equal the reference construction's. The caps tolerate 1.6% (entries) and 3.1% (W7 passes) above the expectations, the success bound no shortfall of the per-group success rate at q3_model (1.4 x 10^-6 after rounding; 0ae69bcb's 2% pad is left out), about one bit with the measured pair term. The organizer experiment vt-ram-r38 checks the counted program's table index, W7 decisions, E17 values and counters on organizer-seeded real first blocks (a code-consistency check and a witness count, not a statistical test).
heuristics.limitations: A premise, not a theorem. The measured events have probability between 2^-27 and 2^-48 per variant, not 2^-105. Only the first block varies between groups; within a group all variants share CV1 (H5). Joint events of two variants on one real chaining value are the premise stated in H5.

heuristics.statement: The average of q3(v) = Pr[rows 16..37 hold | W7 in F7] over the variants the program examines (uniform over the union of the 256 sets R_j) is at least q3_model = 2^-102. Rows 16..22 have the same probability for every valid variant (Lemma 4, exact); only the tail (rows 23..37, through W8, W9, W10 of the variant) is averaged.
heuristics.scope: The expected number of successes per group S = SR p2 q3_model = 2^-68.42135, hence N_G and the success bound 0.3900004.
heuristics.extrapolation: Preregistered sequential Monte-Carlo runs on independent streams (PREREG_v3; smc3.c, proof.md 6.2). R1: 64 runs over a uniform 2^20-variant sample, mean 2^-101.0001, relative sd 0.0230, one-sided 99% bound 2^-101.0101. R2: 256 runs, each with one fresh variant drawn uniformly from the population, mean 2^-100.9983, relative sd 0.0321 (variant dispersion and particle noise together), 99% bound 2^-101.0051 for the population mean. Integer stage factors (-27, -17, -13, -15, -6, -7, -1, tail -15). 1,883,203 tail successes of these runs and of the H5 measurement were rebuilt as 38-step semi-free-start collisions of the variant used and verified (0 failures); on 4,000 of them 0ae69bcb's counted program finds and verifies the pair (4000 of 4000), and the shipped program does so for 4,000 of 4,000 successes of the organizer replica on own seeds (proof.md Appendix C). q3_model is about one bit below both bounds; with the measured pair term the success bound holds down to q3 = 2^-102.99 at the declared N_G, and lowering q3_model by one bit would cost 0.561 in T. Earlier runs whose seeding made consecutive seeds overlapping streams are superseded (their means agree within 0.004 bit). Organizer-executed: vt-q3-smc-r38 runs a reduced replica on organizer seeds; its pass rule (mean of 20 replicates >= 2^-101.45) lies 0.55 bit above q3_model and would fail with probability near 1 if q3 were as low as q3_model.
heuristics.limitations: Monte-Carlo bounds relying on the central limit theorem (64 and 256 estimates); q3 itself (about 2^-101) cannot be observed. Rests on H1 for the distribution of the second-block words.

heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5 the online program is charged by its counted primitives: the model is a 256-bit word RAM whose primitives include 256-bit load or store, and memory is a reported metric with no scalar contribution. A load from any address therefore costs one operation whatever the memory size; the memory used (2^80.12 bytes) is reported. Every table word is written by the counted preprocessing of proof.md 5.1 (2^67.07859 units, charged in time, zero initialisation included).
heuristics.scope: The online cost per (chaining value, A0): one header load and one load per bucket entry instead of a search over 2^29.48 variants.
heuristics.extrapolation: Follows the text of the cost model (computation model, primitive operations, memory scoring). The online and table-construction costs are counted by the interpreter of experiments/vt38.py (selftest items 7, 9 and 10; the table build is checked on a toy instance against the definition of the buckets); vt-ram-r38 reruns the online code on organizer seeds.
heuristics.limitations: The tables are far beyond physical memory. Without unit-cost table access the claim does not hold: finding the buckets through the inverse of s0(u) - u instead of a table gives about 80.68 (proof.md Section 7).

heuristics.statement: The published characteristic, its two-bit conditions and the published dense part S* are advice; the total computation spent to obtain them (failed and repeated searches and tool development included) and all development of this package is at most the fixed allowances A_C = 2^70 units (characteristic search; the paper states the search used an open-source CPU SAT/SMT tool, so the operative hardware ceiling is the CPU branch of the bound chain, 10^5 cores x 10 years = 2^66.6 units, and this charge is ~11x above it), A_S = 2^70 (the Step-1 solve; the paper reports about 2^38.3 compression calls, so the allowance is ~2^31.7 times the published cost) and DEV = 2^64.
heuristics.scope: The allowance part of the ledger (2^71.01123 of T = 2^72.031945) and the advice (below 2^14 bytes).
heuristics.extrapolation: Upper bounds, every factor generous. The paper states the characteristic search ran on an open-source CPU SAT/SMT tool [LLW24a]; GPU lane throughput is not a plausible resource for a CPU solver, so the operative hardware ceiling is the CPU branch of the bound chain: 10^5 CPU cores for 10 years at 10^10 word operations per second = 2^66.6 units, and A_C = 2^70 is 10.6 times it. Cross-checks, each pointing below the charge: the accepted filing 6eeefb64 priced a complete measured re-run of the predecessor 35-step characteristic search with the same tool at 593,858 solver CPU-seconds, times a 32-fold rediscovery factor, times the calibrated price 2^21.677 units per CPU-second = 2^45.86 units; A_C = 2^70 is 2^24.1 times that charge, about 11 million CPU-years, roughly 1,800 times the largest published cryptanalytic computation (SHAttered-scale). The GPU branch (10^4 GPUs for 10 years, 2^73.3 units) is retained for reference as an even more generous bound; a version charging below it on a measured anchor (A_C = 2^68, submission fd3ac033) was reviewed as not evaluable. A_S = 2^70 is 2^31.7 times the paper's published Step-1 figure (about 2^38.3 compression calls): a demonstrated bound. Recorded development of this package below 4.1 x 10^5 CPU-seconds (2^40.5 units). Without allowances T would be 2^71.05; A_C = 2^76 gives 76.06802 and A_C = 2^78 gives 78.01731.
heuristics.limitations: A_C is a bound above the operative CPU-hardware ceiling for the stated SAT/SMT tool, not a measurement of the 38-step search itself; its cost is unpublished and we did not rerun it. The GPU branch of the bound chain is retained only as an even more generous cross-check. A_S and DEV rest on published or recorded figures with wide margins.

heuristics.statement: Let N be the number of successful variants on one chaining value (one group; a real first block's chaining value). The expected number of further successes seen from a success, sum_v Pr[A_v] E[N - 1 | A_v] / sum_v Pr[A_v], is at most delta = 1: on average a success brings at most one further success on the same chaining value. This includes the premise that joint events of two variants on a real chaining value behave as on a uniform one (H1 covers one variant at a time).
heuristics.scope: The group success bound Pr[N >= 1] >= S/2 (Bonferroni with delta = 1; proof.md 6.4), hence N_G and the success bound. Not the validity of any output.
heuristics.extrapolation: Structure: a further success needs a second variant whose own row 16 (2^-27), W7 (2^-3.9) and rows 17..37 (about 2^-74) hold; under independence delta would be about 2^-68. Measurements (proof.md 6.5, preregistered, participant-run): on the chaining values of 513,481 verified successes of variants of 8 A0 spread over the set, every other variant of the 8 A0 not sharing (A0, A1) with the successful one was tested exactly through row 17 (4.5 x 10^7 pairs, 0 cell mismatches); rows 16 and 17 pass at rates consistent with the unconditional ones (row 17: 13 against 11.8 expected); the far term extrapolated to all 256 A0 is at most 0.0018 (99%, seed-clustered). Close variants: 0 further successes on 1,883,203 successes (22.2 x 10^6 trials; 99% bound 2.4 x 10^-6). The budget of 1 is about 500 times the measured value. At q3_model the success bound holds for delta up to 1 (the budget), at the measured q3 for delta up to 1.49; with the measured value as the budget the claim would be 71.64269.
heuristics.limitations: A premise. The measurements are not executed by the organizer; the far term is measured for 8 A0 values and extrapolated; the transfer from the uniform chaining values of semi-free-start successes to real chaining values is supported only indirectly. The budget leaves a margin of about 500 for these.
